messages:
maya: Pushed HF->Redwood conversion of 'mistral-lite-8k' today, benchmark token counts off by ~3-8% on en/wide text
jamal: hmm, token counts drift usually points to tokenizer differences
maya: yeah, dug in — HF tokenizer was created with `normalizer: nfd` and `byte_fallback: true` in the tokenizer JSON. Redwood conversion pipeline applied NFC normalization by default 
li: that can reorder combining marks, right? eg \u00e9 vs e+\u0301
maya: exactly. In some prompt batches we end up with extra space tokens because pre-tokenizer splits on combining sequences differently 
jamal: did this show up in quantization evals or only in perf token counts?
maya: both. When we quantized to int8 we saw a tiny quality regression on chat evals. After aligning normalization the regression mostly disappeared. Suspect tokenization mismatch amplified logits changes after quantization.
li: makes sense. Different token boundaries -> different context windows -> different KV cache alignment -> downstream probability changes :thinking:
maya: quick diff reproducer I used: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('hf-tokenizer.json')
print(t.encode('e\u0301'))
# vs 
from redwood_tokenizer import RedwoodTokenizer
rt = RedwoodTokenizer('converted.json')
print(rt.encode('\u00e9'))
```
maya: also found one config.json mismatch: HF had `add_prefix_space: true` for chat model, but our conversion lost it so messages like " Hello" vs "Hello" changed tokens in chat templates
jamal: ah, prefix space is the classic chat-mode gotcha. We should preserve `add_prefix_space`, `trim_offsets` and `byte_fallback` flags in conversion
li: FYI eval-bot found failing prompt set in convo-regression suite: 12/120 prompts showed >0.5% token-level diff after conversion
eval-bot: auto-diff report attached (summary): changed_token_rate=0.1, mean_token_delta=0.032
maya: plan: add a pre-conversion check that compares HF normalizer pipeline and our target pipeline, and fail conversion if they differ unless user overrides. Also add an optional `--force-preserve-normalizer` flag
jamal: also let's add a small shim to map HF's special tokens fields (`bos_token`, `eos_token`, `unk_token`, `pad_token`) into Redwood config explicitly — saw one case where `eos_token` was in `added_tokens` and got dropped
li: good. For chat templates we should canonicalize system/user/assistant markers and ensure `add_prefix_space` is applied consistently when rendering messages to raw strings
maya: created PR with tests: tokenization parity tests (NFC vs NFD text corpus, with/without prefix space, byte fallback on/off). CI runs on linux + mac and uses the huggingface tokenizers rust wheel to validate
jamal: thanks. Once merged, re-run the quantization experiments and convo-regression suite. If diffs persist we can add a transformer-level adapter that normalizes incoming text before tokenization to avoid changing model weights
li: tiny operational note: some customers send normalized text from frontend (NFKC) — we should document recommended normalization order in onboarding guide
maya: agreed, adding to onboarding checklist and model bring-up playbook. Also logging: conversion should emit a `tokenizer_parity` warning with sample diffs when mismatch detected
jamal: :thumbsup:
